newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt prices mixed, Ecuador Bradies tumble.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt prices mixed, Ecuador Bradies tumble.

text.p: Ecuadoran Bradies tumbled Thursday as political uncertainty and social unrest continued to scare investors away from the market, said emerging debt market sources.
In Ecuador, the 48-hour general strike moved into its second day, as protestors voiced resentment to President Abdala Bucaram's austerity measures.
Ecuador's speaker of Congress, Fabian Alarcon, called legislators to a special session -- scheduled at 1700 EST/2300 GMT on Thursday -- to determine Bucaram's political fate.
In his public address to the nation Thursday afternoon, Bucaram said he would take "all powers" necessary if the constitutional order was threatened.

"The government makes clear that in the case of an attempt to break with constitutional order, I will assume all of the powers available to protect the legitimacy of the popular will and the national judicial order," Bucaram said.
In addition, he announced the resignations of several cabinet ministers including Energy Minister Alfredo Adum.
Analysts and traders said the political and social unrest in Ecuador had definitely taken its toll on the country's debt instruments.
Walter Molano, director of economic and financial research for Latin America at SBC Warburg in New York, said the country's current quandary "is unleashing a lot of uncertainty into the market."
Indeed, Ecuadoran Brady bonds took a third straight day of beatings.
